subject: Coordination: multi-team architecture sync (VPC connectivity + IAM) for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme-retail.com>, Dinesh Kumar <dinesh.kumar@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed architecture sync — ACME pilot (VPC + on‑prem connectivity, IAM)

Hi Sarah / Dinesh —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, the next step is a focused architecture review to align on VPC connectivity options, on‑prem networking, and IAM/auth flows so engineering and security can sign off for the pilot. We want the following folks in the session:

- ACME: networking engineer(s), security owner, procurement (for procurement questions)
- Redwood: myself (AE), Soojin (SE, networking/IAM lead), Aditya (Eng manager)

Suggested slots (all PDT):
- Tue June 15, 10:00–11:00
- Wed June 16, 13:00–14:00
- Thu June 17, 09:00–10:00

Agenda (draft):
1) Introductions & objectives (5m)
2) VPC connectivity options: VPC peering vs. VPN vs. PrivateLink (20m)
3) On‑prem networking requirements (NAT, egress IPs, firewall rules) (15m)
4) IAM & access model (service accounts, key management, audit logs) (15m)
5) Action items / next steps (5m)

I attached a short agenda and a requested list of network artifacts that will make the session productive. If you prefer different times, please propose alternatives and we can coordinate. Also, if procurement/legal want to triage SOW/PO items before the call we can include a short slot.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Proposed architecture sync — ACME pilot (VPC + on‑prem connectivity, IAM)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few notes from ACME side:

- Preferred time: Thu June 17, 09:00–10:00 PDT works best for our network team (they need time to pull the diagrams).
- Attendees: myself (security), Dinesh Kumar (network lead), Priya N. (procurement, procurement@acme-retail.com), and two of our infra engineers (will add on reply).
- Prep: we can share our high‑level network diagram and existing IAM roles; Dinesh will post the diagram by EOD Friday.

One ask from security: please include a short slide on audit/logging retention and how Redwood handles keys (KMS/HSM integration). If Soojin can cover that, great.

We don’t need a lengthy SOW discussion in the first call; procurement prefers a follow‑up after we confirm technical fit.

—Sarah
Sarah Jensen
Senior Security Architect, ACME Retail

Subject: Re: Proposed architecture sync — ACME pilot (VPC + on‑prem connectivity, IAM)

Thanks Sarah — glad Thu 17th works. I’ll cover KMS/HSM roadmap, audit/logging retention options, and the IAM model we recommend for an initial pilot. A few quick prep asks so we can keep the call concrete: 

1) Can you share the network diagram (Dinesh mentioned EOD Friday) — the PNG in Marissa’s note is a stub but if you have a CIDR map and firewall egress list that would be ideal.
2) Any proxy / outbound filtering (e.g., forced corporate proxy) or TLS-inspecting devices on the path? That affects our recommended connectivity.
3) Expected sequence length/typical payloads (helps size KV cache and batching sizing).

I've attached a focused 1‑page agenda and a sample allowlist table (public egress IPs we’ll ask you to allow if you choose direct egress). If you prefer PrivateLink or a managed VPN we’ll show config differences during the call.

Proposed owners / timebox on the call:
- Intro & objectives — Marissa (5m)
- Network topology & constraints — Dinesh (10m)
- Redwood connectivity options (SE) — Soojin (15m)
- IAM & key management — Soojin (10m)
- Ops & audit/retention — Aditya (10m)
- Open Q/A & next steps — all (10m)

Attachments: redwood-deep-dive-agenda.pdf (updated v2, 130KB); acme-network-topology.png (placeholder)

—Soojin
